Fun fact: before the dairy farms, the Plateau grew beer. In the 1880s Enumclaw went through what historians call a "hop craze" — the fields around town grew hops for brewers until hop lice and a market crash sent the farmers to cows. And when the town was platted in 1885, the founders gave away a lot for a saloon before almost anything else.

Who's behind the bar

A sommelier and a Cicerone walk into a wine shop.

In August 2019, Mikey and Lyra Penoyer bought Plateau Wines, the wine shop that had anchored this block of Cole Street for four years. Lyra had one condition: "add more beer."

She had the credentials to ask. In 2013 she became the 13th person — and the third woman — in Washington to pass the Certified Cicerone exam, the four-hour beer equivalent of a sommelier's test. Mikey is the wine side: the one driving back from Walla Walla with the trunk full, the one who curates the club.

So the name changed, the taps went in, a to-go cooler filled up in the back, and the shop became the only room in town where a Belgian lambic and a grand cru Burgundy sit on the same bar — with two people who can tell you exactly why.

The room

Part bottle shop, part living room, part game night.

Part of the room is shelves, part of it is stools, and there's a Go board on the bar. The art on the walls is a different local artist every month.

Find us

Under the sign that says all four things.

Wine, beer, food, bottle shop, bar — it's on the sign. Historic downtown, between the shops, street parking out front.

  • Small plates at the barHummus plate, margherita flatbread, crab rangoon, a cucumber sandwich.
